body:
## User-facing outcome

Extend `rcf` to prove statements about one real variable with real algebraic coefficients and caller-registered real constants. For an algebraic coefficient, the chosen real root matters: “a root of x²−2” must distinguish +√2 from −√2. For a registered constant such as π, the caller supplies approximations and proofs about those approximations.

This issue connects the mathematical libraries to Lean syntax, the decision procedure and the resulting proof. It is part of #10331 / #10143. The [tactic SPEC](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/blob/main/HexRCF/SPEC/hex-rcf.md#planned-real-coefficient-extension) and [shared execution contract](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/blob/main/SPEC/real-closure-execution.md) give the full requirements.

The formula representation (#10338), mechanism for registering tactic handlers (#10359), and preparation of source coefficients/divisor conditions (#10368) are merged. Reuse them. They do not by themselves provide the numerical solver.

## Tactic and manual contract

1. Select a small set of statements with the library owners. Keep rational regression examples, but also require algebraic-coefficient examples that actually use the new code. Include decisions at roots and between roots, a false statement, and an unsupported or invalid input.
2. Connect coefficient evaluation, root/sign calculations and certificate checking using the functions already available in #10375/#10377/#10378. Use #10376 when the examples need registered constants. Add only the missing functionality required by these examples.
3. Exercise the path from the user's statement to the answer and proposed proof. Build representative examples and audit proof dependencies. Measure tactic cost when it answers a named implementation question or investigates an observed bottleneck, using the existing tools.
4. This issue alone owns the real-coefficient rcf manual and tactic examples. Extend the existing rcf manual chapter (`HexManual/Chapters/HexRCF.lean`), retaining its current examples and documenting the optional import, new examples, diagnostics, running times and proof limitations. Fix failures and impractical running times. Preserve delivered examples and continue with the remaining API/manual coverage below.

A useful candidate is `∀ x : ℝ, x^2 - 2 * Real.sqrt 2 * x + 2 ≥ 0`. A later example requiring a further algebraic root is `∃ x : ℝ, x^2 = Real.sqrt 2 ∧ 1 < x ∧ x < 2`. Confirm that the selected examples exercise the intended implementation, rather than being solved entirely by the old rational path.

Ordinary real sample points are sufficient to start. Users need not mention infinitesimals, and the complete infinitesimal tower need not be ready. If an algorithm does use them internally, a real conclusion still needs a proof that one real point satisfies the entire finite set of conditions.

The shared query semantics are proved: #10389 closed through #10521, and the
current Tau Ceti pin also contains Thom/BKR and ordered real-closure existence.
There is no admission exception. Preserve the handler's rejection of every
`sorryAx` dependency and ordinary kernel checking for both rational and new
coefficient paths. Use the actual merged theorems rather than waiting for the
broader Tau Ceti roadmap.

## Ready-to-assign continuation

The existing manual already contains square-root and cubic aliases, selected
Hex roots, QAdjoin arithmetic, independent square roots and a degree-six
common-field example (#10424, #10428, #10470, #10472). Preserve these and do not
restart Stage 1. This issue owns the remaining source-conversion coverage,
common-field certification coverage, caller-registered constants, general
build/check path, algebraic-only completeness, diagnostics and documentation.

Start now with source authentication and a caller-registered-constant path
using the delivered #10376 interface. Keep the approximation computation,
requested-width proof and containment proof separate. First exercise the
actual prepare/build/check/proof path on a supplied registration, a cancelled
zero denominator and deliberately uninformative bounds. This is a focused
integration experiment, not a request for a bundled analytic provider.
Resolve a concrete contract gap in the owning SPEC before implementing a
changed contract; discuss substantial architecture changes with the user.

Use ordinary real samples where sufficient. Completion of the general
infinitesimal path consumes #10378's finite-sign realization and #10377's total
root interfaces; those are completion dependencies, not a reason to defer
independent work here. The #10377/#10378 workers own their library files.
Coordinate any needed API, do not duplicate it. Keep this issue open until
all required implementation, tests and documentation below are complete.

## Algebraic-number and fixed-field inputs

Direct use of the existing Hex types is a required part of the adapter, not an optional demonstration. Accept fixed, reconstructible `RealAlgebraicNumber.toReal` values obtained from checked real `AlgebraicNumber` constructions, and real values of elements computed in `QAdjoin a`. The latter may use the existing `toAlgebraicNumber` conversion, checked reality and `toReal`, with proofs preserving the chosen embedding. `QAdjoin.value_real` supplies the reality fact when the generator is real. Do not assume a `QAdjoin.toReal` method already exists. Provide the necessary proved connection to the coefficient interface without inventing a new number-field representation.

Retain the delivered example whose coefficient is a nonquadratic algebraic root and another using arithmetic in `QAdjoin`. For example, let α be the selected real root of X³−X−1 and compute β=α²−1 in its fixed field; prove `∀ x : ℝ, x/α = β*x` after the checked real conversions. Show the complete Hex construction in the manual, not just real symbols with assumed identities. `Real.sqrt` examples exercise aliases for this general support, not a special solver for radicals.

Retain a Mathlib higher-degree real-root alias alongside `Real.sqrt`, for example `(2 : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)` as the positive cube root of 2. Prove its equality with the selected Hex algebraic root of X³−2 and use it in a genuine tactic example such as `∀ x : ℝ, x^2 + (2 : ℝ)^(1 / 3 : ℝ)*x + 1 > 0`. The pinned Mathlib's `Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow` and positivity results support that identification. Show the supported alias and setup in the manual. This permits closed algebraic coefficients, not real powers of the quantified variable or an unchecked signed-root interpretation for negative bases.

For Stage 2, include coefficients from independently constructed fields and root-finding over an existing real number field. Reuse existing conversion/common-field results and retain the selected roots. Reject nonreal coefficients and incorrect root identifications; complex conjugation fixes a real number and does not select a different real conjugate. These are fixed coefficients in goals quantified over ℝ, not arbitrary parameters or quantification over `QAdjoin`.

## Required implementation

1. **Extend the existing tactic.** Keep the same `rcf` command and the existing rational solver. `import HexRCF` retains current behavior; the optional `HexRCF.RealCoefficients` import enables the extension. Retain rational compatibility, deterministic handler selection, restoration of state after a handler declines, and checks that a returned proof proves the original goal. Reject every `sorryAx` dependency in the new extension as in the existing solver. Keep the published base library independent of the real-closure libraries.
2. **Use the specified optional adapter.** Put `HexRCF.RealCoefficients` under `adapters/`, in namespace `Hex.RCF.RealCoefficients`, with the Coefficients/Specialize/Replay/Soundness/Reify modules as needed. Include it in the default `HexRCFRealCoefficients` Lake target and library metadata. Reuse the shared formula syntax; no second formula language or Mathlib companion is needed. Release wiring is outside scope.
3. **Recognize and authenticate coefficients.** Support rational and real algebraic constants, registered closed real constants, arithmetic, natural powers and division by closed expressions. An alias such as `Real.sqrt 2` needs a proof identifying the chosen positive root. Reject arbitrary parameters/functions and division depending on the quantified variable. Preserve every original nonzero-divisor condition before simplification, even under cancellation or multiplication by zero. Rewrite `p(x)/c` as `p(x)*c⁻¹` before extracting closed coefficients so parameter denominators do not reach the shared integer formula translator.
4. **Construct the polynomial formula.** Implement `Coefficients.prepare` and `Specialize.prepare` using ordinary total arithmetic and `DensePoly`. Group terms by the exponent of the variable, evaluate their coefficient expressions, and prove evaluation and degree are preserved. Reuse the shared QF/Prenex/Boolean traversal and its equivalence for every coefficient assignment, then specialize it to the authenticated coefficients and original goal. Support exactly one variable and one quantifier, over ℝ or `(a,b]` with literal dyadic endpoints. Encode the latter using the existing inequality atoms, without a new domain representation.
5. **Compute roots, intervals and a certificate.** Find the complete union of relevant polynomial roots, remove duplicates and evaluate the formula at roots and on intervening intervals. Implement `build` and `Replay.check`/`check`. Bind evidence to the exact sentence, coefficient order, registered subjects, versions and root representations. Check all original divisor conditions even for constant, zero or empty-domain cases. Certificate checking verifies recorded identities and evidence; it must not rerun root isolation, gcd, BKR or approximation searches.
6. **Prove that acceptance proves the original statement.** Prove `check_domains` and `check_sound`, using the actual arithmetic and root correctness theorems. Root coverage, polynomial degree, domains, nested sign calculations and real sample existence must be established, not added as unproved assumptions. Emit an ordinary Lean-kernel proof. A compiled Boolean answer, external oracle or approximation callback is not proof evidence. Preserve the half-open interval endpoints; the shared Tarski queries have their own open, root-free endpoint conditions.
7. **Prove the required termination and completeness.** Complete the algebraic-only decision procedure and prove it produces accepted certificates. General searches with named constants need correct shrinking bounds and transcendence over the entire preceding field. Individual certified successes do not require a general convergence or transcendence theorem, but still need correct bounds. Such successes do not turn partial coefficient comparisons into the total field operations required by generic root algorithms.
8. **Provide clear failure behavior.** Distinguish an invalid input, an invalid certificate, a false statement and an interrupted or unresolved search. A false answer is a diagnostic, not a proof of the original goal. Do not swallow arbitrary exceptions and silently try a different method. Preserve failures through Boolean and quantifier evaluation as specified.

## Stage 2: document the additional capabilities

As the required #10377 APIs merge, extend the same manual with runnable examples of simultaneous polynomial sign conditions, distinguishing and ordering algebraic roots, evaluating signs at a selected root, and comparing roots defined by different polynomials. Include common roots or repeated roots in the input where supported by the consuming algorithms. Explain the mathematical use of each capability and ensure the examples actually exercise it. For library operations without a natural tactic example, provide a direct API example. Check the examples, record representative running times and audit the actual transitive proof dependencies; no admission remains permitted. Preserve the existing examples and keep the documentation a coherent account of one `rcf` tactic.

## Mathematics supplied by other issues

- #10375 supplies the shared polynomial/query computation; #10389 has supplied its proved general interpretation as sums of signs over roots.
- #10377 supplies complete sign patterns and Thom root identity/order. #10378 supplies selected-root arithmetic, root/interval samples, conversion after representation changes, and proofs about real samples.
- #10376 supplies bounds and sign calculations for caller-registered constants. The caller supplies the constant-specific containment proofs. General termination also needs shrinking bounds and relative transcendence; separate transcendence of constants does not establish their joint independence.
- Actual Tau Ceti existence of an ordered algebraic real closure is needed for the general infinitesimal model. Direct reasoning with ordinary real samples does not need that existence theorem, but still needs the relevant real-root correctness proofs. The required existence theorem is supplied by the current Tau Ceti pin; use its actual hypotheses, not roadmap status.

Use the particular merged functions and proved results that an example needs. Do not wait for unrelated performance work or duplicate mathematics owned by these libraries. The virtual-substitution issue #10329 is not a dependency.

## Final tests and evidence

Build with Lake and preserve the repository's dependency, umbrella and relative-link checks. Test handler order, malformed signatures, proofs of the wrong goal, state restoration after decline/failure, and terminal false/interrupted/replay failures. Check aliases in both equality orientations, compound coefficients, missing or cyclic aliases, and variable-dependent replacements. Substitution must preserve every original divisor condition.

Required fully proved examples include both selected roots of x²−2, a checked square-root alias, and registered constants with correctly preserved divisor conditions. The specified examples involving `∀ x, x² > π−4`, `∀ x, x²+e>2`, `∃ x, x=e ∧ 2<x ∧ x<3`, and `1/(4−π)` assume caller-supplied registrations and bounds. Implementing those providers is not part of this issue.

Cover zero/constant polynomials, cancellation of leading terms, all comparisons and Boolean forms, repeated/common roots, wrong conjugates, endpoint/equal/reversed domains, outdated or swapped root/constant evidence, cyclic dependencies, omitted BKR sign patterns and interruption. Refuse division by zero even when cancelled, including `0/(π−π)`. An interval containing zero without proving equality or a strict sign is insufficient; test refusal with deliberately uninformative approximation procedures.

Check proof dependencies in fresh modules. Existing rational examples and fully verified results must remain free of `sorryAx`, new axioms and `native_decide`. All new examples must satisfy the same axiom restrictions. Keep numerical
measurements Mathlib-free. Follow the current PLAN/Phase4.md proof track:
representative tactic/certificate examples built in CI, not mandatory sweeps
of ordinary theorem applications. Targeted proof-cost experiments must answer
a named quotation/sharing/sample-selection question or investigate an observed
bottleneck. This adapter owns conformance and build-only proof/tactic examples for
coefficient production and specialization. Its Mathlib-importing authentication,
specialization and proof construction must not be imported by an executable
benchmark. Measure the owners' Mathlib-free primitives on adapter-generated
inputs where appropriate, clearly excluding adapter preparation from that
measurement. Do not require a core split merely to obtain an executable
timing; specify and coordinate any genuinely reusable core extraction first. Vary degree, atom count,
coefficient size, precision and depth independently; include bounded failures,
common/repeated roots, memory, unique DAG nodes and expanded work. Quotation
must preserve sharing or account for expansion. Other algorithm scaling stays
with its owners; old rational-tactic timings are not evidence for
this extension. Retain completed measurements and their limitations.


## Scope and delivery

Reuse the shared coefficient rules: one stored zero, possibly several representations of other values, mathematical equality tested by a zero difference, and exact bindings to the intended representation. Changes of defining polynomials require explicit conversion of affected values and rejection of outdated evidence. Do not invent field instances on raw syntax, fallible arithmetic interfaces or per-operation certificate frameworks.

HexInterval, bundled π/e procedures, constant-specific analytic work, full CAD/coverings, multivariate/nested quantifier elimination, nonstandard analysis, algebraic-independence claims and publication are excluded. Keep reusable arithmetic and certificate checking with their library owners.

Partial PRs use `Refs` and record remaining work for #10331. Immediately after opening a PR, request Claude Opus review using $second-opinion while CI runs. Address review findings, conflicts and failures. Discuss substantial changes of architecture with the user. Merge green with `gh pr merge --squash --auto` without `--delete-branch`. Do not edit AGENTS.md/PLAN.md or add CI jobs. Report a false statement or missing mathematical hypothesis rather than weakening the claim. Editing this issue does not launch workers or monitoring.

This issue also owns phase/evidence attestation for the optional adapter's
implemented surface. #10575 audits integrated documentation and imports but
does not independently implement this tactic or rewrite its examples.

comments.body: Claiming the ready base registry tranche on branch issue-10358 under coordinator #10331. I will implement typed coefficient recognition, checked deterministic handler registration, transactional dispatch and focused regressions; later adapter integration remains gated on coordinator-verified artifacts. This tranche will use Refs and leave this issue open.

Shared frontend milestone verified: PR #10338 merged as `843102b505b61724a9679d0011afb6d662812b92`. Main exports `RealFormula.Reify.reify`/`reify!` with Result source/proof, and the optional integer adapter's `toSentence_correct`, `residue_correct`, `check_sound`. HexRealFormula and HexRealFormulaMathlib are both admitted through Phase 1 in libraries.yml.

The frontend part of the later milestone is now available. After the current base-handler tranche, you may proceed with independently supported source-schema/abstraction work against these actual declarations. Generic coefficient specialization still needs #10333's applicable records, and the provider/tower/replay gates remain explicit. Do not wait for virtual substitution #10329 or infer generic coefficient support from the integer adapter. Reconcile builds with the new default adapter target on main.

<!-- hex-rcf-family-monitor -->

Base tranche PR: #10359, head `6b7691f807a9aeb33cee177d559d516208682116`. Fresh Claude Opus review and CI are running. The local affected builds, new handler regressions, axiom guards, DAG/umbrella checks and source checks pass. Rebased onto the shared-frontend milestone and built the new default `HexRCFRealFormula` adapter successfully.

The implemented surface is `Reify.UnsupportedCoefficient` / `recognizeSentence`, `HandlerResult` / `Handler`, `@[rcf_handler]`, deterministic `handlerNames`, and transactional `proveGoal` / `rcf`. The base still imports no family or optional adapter. No real-coefficient decision support is claimed.

I have read the newly authorized source-schema continuation against the actual shared reifier: `Hex.RealFormula.Reify.Result.proof` supplies the all-valuation equivalence and `Result.source` is the valuation-indexed source. Closed-expression abstraction can instantiate that equivalence independently of generic coefficient arithmetic. Its continuation must still collect original divisor guards and rewrite variable numerators over closed denominators before shared reification; the shared parser deliberately rejects parameter denominators. #10333's generic arithmetic and the provider/tower/replay gates remain separate.

Fresh Opus review of #10359 identified a concrete SPEC/dispatch integration gap requiring coordinator clarification before adapter work proceeds:

- The current directive requires dispatch **only** for unsupported **closed coefficient syntax**, and rejects arbitrary symbolic parameters.
- `HexRCF/SPEC/hex-rcf.md` also says local symbols may be accepted when an explicit equality identifies them with a closed coefficient.
- For `(a : ℝ) (h : a = Real.pi) ⊢ ∀ x : ℝ, x + a = x + a`, rational recognition currently sees the free variable `a`, so no closed-coefficient handler runs. Merely registering the future adapter cannot implement the SPEC's local-equality case.

Dropping the free-variable check would dispatch arbitrary parameters and contradict the ready tranche's boundary, so I will not silently widen it. A base preprocessing/recognition bridge for explicit equalities, or an explicit requirement to rewrite/substitute these equalities before `rcf`, is needed. Please clarify the intended contract on this same issue; no decomposition issue is needed. I have paused the independent source-schema scratch work at this boundary.

Other review findings are independently actionable: preserve successful handlers' auxiliary declarations while rolling back target/metavariable assignments; extend existential/Ioc/registration regressions; make the IO-ref test harness explicitly synchronous. I am addressing those in #10359. The issue remains open and no real-coefficient support is claimed.

Decision: preserve the SPEC's automatic explicit-equality case. Do not require users to rewrite manually, and do not admit arbitrary symbolic parameters. The directive's phrase “closed coefficient syntax” includes a coefficient identified with a closed expression by an explicit local equality proof; the missing base recognition bridge is in scope for this issue.

Concretely, extend the typed recognition boundary to retain/check equality witnesses for local real coefficient symbols (either `h : a = c` or `h : c = a`) where the replacement is independent of the quantified variable and contains no unresolved metavariables or unaccounted-for free real parameters. Handle compound coefficient expressions by substituting their eligible symbols. A simple direct local equality to a closed expression suffices; no generic assumption solving, arbitrary simp search, or claimed transcendence is required. Reject missing/nonclosed/cyclic bindings. The base checks proof/type/closedness and routes the unchanged original target; the optional handler remains responsible for the supported closed grammar and proof-producing substitution. A checked preprocessing equivalence is also acceptable if the result is transported back and checked against the original target.

Keep source divisions intact while finding aliases: do not simplify or cancel before collecting original guards. For example, `h : a = π-π` must not let the future extension accept `0/a`; `h : a = π` does allow the reviewer’s example to reach the handler. Equality to an expression depending on the bound variable is not a fixed coefficient. Unauthenticated free symbols still decline/raise the terminal unsupported-parameter diagnostic; ordinary false/replay/exhaustion outcomes still never dispatch.

Please clarify the owning SPEC's dispatch paragraph in the same PR, distinguishing syntactically closed coefficients from these equality-certified aliases. Add regressions for both orientations, compound aliases, missing/nonclosed bindings and failed-attempt state restoration. For the base tranche a dedicated ordinary-proof test handler verifies routing and the original-target proof; do not claim the numerical adapter is implemented. Continue the independently actionable review fixes and then the already-authorized source-schema work. No decomposition or further approval is needed.

Base registry tranche landed: #10359, squash commit `b1a8702aea9ed3492629c1506b50aea822d16826`. Required CI run [35514342110](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/actions/runs/35514342110) completed successfully, including library/conformance/manual builds and bench/oracle gates. Merged with `gh pr merge --squash --auto`; branch retained.

Exact delivered surface:
- `HexRCF/Reify.lean`: `ClosedCoefficient`, `UnsupportedCoefficient`, public `closeCoefficient?` and typed `recognizeSentence`; direct checked equality aliases in either orientation, compound substitution and unchanged divisor syntax.
- `HexRCF/Tactic.lean`: `HandlerResult`, `Handler`, global checked `@[rcf_handler]`, deduplicated `Name.lt` order, transactional `proveGoal`/`rcf`, original-target validation and transitive ordinary-axiom allowlist. Success retains necessary declarations/kernel tasks; decline/failure restores state. Rational false/replay/runtime failures never dispatch.
- `HexRCF/HandlerTests/{Support,Async}.lean` and `HexRCF/HandlerTests.lean`: deterministic dispatch, malformed signatures, wrong/ill-typed/unresolved/compiler-trusting proofs, direct/transitive forbidden axioms, goal/metavariable restoration, terminal outcomes, aliases, endpoints and asynchronous auxiliary declarations. Published test metadata includes them.

Fresh Opus reviews were completed and substantive findings addressed; [review resolution](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/pull/10359#issuecomment-5750179461). Ordinary generated theorem axiom audits and affected local/structural checks pass. This adds no numerical real-coefficient solver or new family import.

The coordinator-authorized independent source-schema continuation is prepared and locally validated against merged shared frontend #10338. It will ship as a separate Refs tranche. Generic coefficient/tower integration remains paused under the latest coordinator boundary: no PolyOps/#10348 consumption, no HexInterval, and future transcendental evidence is caller supplied. Authentication, specialization, root/cell replay, soundness/progress, selected-root reconstruction and complete extension conformance/performance evidence remain gated on settled actual owner APIs. Issue stays open; downstream dispatch remains with #10331.

Independent frontend/source-schema tranche is now PR #10368, head `90adf9302f70f0543ccddd361d5782a8b0c160e8`. A fresh Opus review was started immediately after opening; CI [35517257731](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/actions/runs/35517257731) is running.

`Hex.RCF.RealCoefficients.Reify.prepare` supplies a fixed-valuation shared `Prenex` schema and an ordinary-kernel equivalence to the original source. It retains pending divisor obligations before cancellation/abstraction and uses checked alias substitution. The default optional target, CI cache/build list, conformance coverage and manual are wired. It imports no HexInterval, consumes no PolyOps, registers no solver and provides no numerical authentication or guard discharge. Five named schema theorem axiom audits, affected Lake builds, structural checks and 19 relative paths/anchors pass locally.

The coordinator owns the unsettled SPEC/architecture correction, so this tranche has no SPEC edits. Dependent integration remains paused; issue #10358 stays open.

Independent source-schema tranche landed: #10368, squash commit `75e903f08e93521685cc6a11355a84333931c2dd`. Required CI run [35518667559](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/actions/runs/35518667559) completed successfully. Merged with `gh pr merge --squash --auto`; branch `issue-10358` retained.

Exact delivered artifacts:
- `adapters/HexRCF/RealCoefficients{.lean,/Reify.lean}`: `Hex.RCF.RealCoefficients.Reify.Source` and `prepare`, using the actual merged shared `Hex.RealFormula` frontend. Preparation returns the fixed coefficient order/valuation, shared Prenex formula, pending original-divisor obligations after checked alias substitution, budget usage, and an ordinary-kernel proof `Prenex.toProp formula valuation ↔ original`.
- Closed-source arithmetic recognition includes rationals, π, literal `Real.exp 1`, arithmetic, natural powers and closed division. Variable-bearing division becomes multiplication by the closed inverse before maximal coefficient abstraction. Guards survive zero multiplication and cancellation. This is source recognition only: it does not authenticate numerical coefficients or discharge nonzero obligations.
- One real binder and whole-real/literal-dyadic Ioc restrictions are enforced on the original source. Ioc remains shared guard atoms; checked aliases reuse the base-owned `closeCoefficient?`. Unsupported functions, variable denominators, noncanonical operations and unresolved source metavariables are refused.
- Default build target `HexRCFRealCoefficients` (`srcDir := adapters`), optional umbrella, DAG/library metadata, existing single-job CI build/cache list, README and manual wiring. Published base umbrella remains independent of this adapter; publication wiring was not added.
- `conformance/HexRCF/RealCoefficientsConformance.lean`: guard/order/budget/alias/domain/state regressions and five named ordinary-kernel schema theorems (`piSchema`, `expSchema`, `aliasSchema`, `quotientSchema`, `intervalSchema`), each audited for only the three standard axioms. These are equivalence proofs, not the final numerical π/e goals.

The fresh post-opening Opus review found no correctness or soundness blockers; [resolution and documentation clarifications](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/pull/10368#issuecomment-5750641669). Affected Lake builds (including the manual), DAG/umbrella/manifest/trust checks, 37 structural unit tests, 19 relative links/anchors and `git diff --check` passed locally, followed by required CI on the final revision. No new axioms, sorry proofs or native_decide were introduced. AGENTS.md and PLAN.md were not edited.

Together with base registry PR #10359 at `b1a8702aea9ed3492629c1506b50aea822d16826`, these are complete independent tranches, not completion of #10358. Remaining work includes authenticated coefficient preparation, specialization/evaluation/degree proofs, selected-root and sqrt reconstruction, root/cell construction and literal replay, original-guard discharge, domain/soundness/realization and progress laws, final numerical proofs, and full extension conformance/measurement evidence.

Generic coefficient/tower integration remains paused under the coordinator's current boundary: no PolyOps/#10348 consumption, no HexInterval, and caller-supplied approximation/containment/progress evidence for future transcendental coefficients. The coordinator owns the settled architecture and downstream dispatch. This issue remains open for resumption against actual authorized owner APIs.

Coordinator audit: the owning terminal session has stopped at its account usage limit. No worker is currently progressing this issue; remaining generic integration stays held. The delivered SPEC section is incorporated into the coordinator-owned correction PR #10365.

<!-- hex-rcf-family-monitor -->

PR #10413 makes the existing `rcf` cell proofs reusable for algebraic coefficients. It proves partition, ordering, polynomial sign constancy and universal/existential evaluation for cells defined by a finite ordered list of real roots, and routes the rational solver through those same proofs while preserving its public interfaces. It adds no admissions and changes no executable certificate checker. Local rational regression tests and ordinary axiom checks pass; Fable found no blockers, and its useful documentation/import/test suggestions have been addressed. CI remains pending.

This is preparation for the Stage 1 solver, not a working algebraic tactic demo. Source coefficient authentication, complete algebraic root/sign certificate assembly and checking, handler registration, the narrow #10389 admission allowance, and runnable manual examples with timings remain outstanding. PRs #10411 (coefficient preparation) and #10412 (shared query interpretation under the recorded #10389 exception) also remain in CI.

PR #10411 now includes checked translation from user-written closed real coefficients to expressions using Hex's existing real algebraic arithmetic. It preserves direct `RealAlgebraicNumber` and converted `QAdjoin` values, recognizes square and higher roots, and proves the equality back to the original expression. The selected embedding is preserved. Original divisor checks remain visible before simplification.

Local examples cover mixed square and cube roots, a nonquadratic algebraic coefficient, arithmetic in its number field, equivalent higher-root notation, unsupported inputs, missing sign proofs and resource limits. The generated equality proofs have only the ordinary logical axioms. Claude Fable found no soundness blocker; the diagnostic, proof-visibility and test findings have been addressed. CI is running on the updated PR.

These are coefficient-translation examples, not yet the requested `rcf` tactic demo. Literal certificate authentication, divisor discharge, final root/sign and decision replay, handler registration, and the runnable manual examples and end-to-end timings remain outstanding for Stage 1. The separate local isolation and selected-root work is preserved. No new admission has been introduced or assigned to #10389.

The algebraic coefficient preparation tranche has merged as #10411. It translates closed `RealAlgebraicNumber`, checked `Real.sqrt`/higher `Real.rpow`, and arithmetic expressions to the existing algebraic-number operations with ordinary proofs of their real values; it includes the selected-embedding conversion for `QAdjoin` and polynomial specialization. This is source preparation, not a usable `rcf` extension yet: literal coefficient-sign authentication, checked decision assembly, and the optional handler remain open. The existing rational `rcf` path is unchanged.

The formula evaluator (#10414), narrow #10389 admission audit (#10415), and checked real-root isolation (#10416) are under review/CI as separate partial #10377 contributions. No new work on #10389 is needed for these computational steps.

Stage 1 progress: #10414 is merged. It proves that a formula’s truth follows from checked signs of its polynomial atoms, including all Boolean branches. This is a component of the existing `rcf` extension; the tactic is not yet usable on algebraic coefficients. The root-isolation, atom-product and repeated-root replay pieces are in #10416, #10417 and #10418. Local integration now produces and checks complete cell-sign rows, but the tactic still needs a compact, kernel-checkable representation of selected algebraic roots and field coordinates. Direct kernel reduction of a cubic canonical value was too costly even for a small sign or stored-enclosure equality. I am working on that representation bridge without touching #10389; its one named root-sum admission remains the only planned exception.

Stage 1 update: #10424 has merged. Importing the optional `HexRCF.RealCoefficients` adapter now extends the existing `rcf` command with runnable selected algebraic coefficients; the rational solver remains in place. The integrated manual and conformance cover `Real.sqrt 2`, the cubic real-power alias, Hex's checked selected cubic root, and a coefficient computed with ordinary `QAdjoin` arithmetic, plus existential, false and unsupported inputs. The report `reports/hex-rcf-algebraic-demo.md` records end-to-end module timings and independent numerical checks. The algebraic proofs depend on the single named root-sum admission in #10389; the rational examples do not.

#10426 is in CI after Fable review and adds a proved `ZPoly.rootNear`/selected-root identity and a second cubic manual example. #10427 is in CI and review with further BKR/Thom and algebraic-field examples.
